zh.title: 新加坡航空777-9推進首飛準備　消息指煞車與滑行測試已完成
zh.summary: 消息指新加坡航空777-9新機WH291（N20092）已完成煞車與滑行測試，首飛暫定10月14日；相關安排尚未獲波音或新加坡航空官方確認，亦不代表已完成首飛或交付。
body: 新加坡航空訂購之一架波音777-9新機正推進首次飛行準備。據航空動態消息指出，機體代號WH291、使用美國註冊編號N20092的航機，已於上個週末完成煞車與滑行測試，首飛暫定安排於10月14日，實際時程仍須依測試整備狀況與作業需求調整。目前尚未取得波音或新加坡航空對該首飛安排的官方確認。
航空攝影師Hongming Zheng於2026年10月10日在美國華盛頓州潘恩機場（PAE）拍攝的照片，已記錄到這架N20092。照片資料將機型列為777-9，攝影師並註明機身可見新加坡航空塗裝元素、翼尖處於折起狀態，提供了該機近期地面活動的影像紀錄。
煞車與滑行測試屬於新機首飛前的地面檢查，用於確認航機在地面移動、操控與減速時的系統表現。依所提供的更新內容，10月14日仍是暫定日期，不能視為該機已完成首飛；本次所稱「首飛」也僅指這架航機的首次飛行。
777-9是波音777X系列的大型雙發廣體客機，採用GE9X發動機與折疊翼尖設計。依波音公布的規格，機身長76.7公尺，翼展在展開時為71.8公尺，地面折起翼尖後縮減至64.8公尺，以兼顧飛行效率與機場地面設施的使用需求。
個別生產機完成首次飛行，仍不等於已交付航空公司或具備投入載客服務的條件。波音於2026年公布的777-9測試進度指出，除專用試飛機外，採生產構型的航機也參與認證工作，當時預計於2027年開始交付。WH291後續的測試、交付與營運安排，仍有待官方進一步公布。

en.title: Singapore Airlines 777-9 Advances Toward First Flight as Reports Indicate Brake and Taxi Tests Completed
en.summary: Reports indicate Singapore Airlines 777-9 WH291, registered N20092, has completed brake and taxi tests, with a first flight tentatively set for October 14. Neither Boeing nor Singapore Airlines has officially confirmed the schedule, and it does not establish that the aircraft has flown or been delivered.
body: A Boeing 777-9 ordered by Singapore Airlines is progressing toward its first flight. According to aviation updates, the aircraft, identified as WH291 and carrying U.S. registration N20092, completed brake and taxi tests last weekend. Its first flight is tentatively scheduled for October 14, subject to testing readiness and operational requirements. No official confirmation of this first-flight schedule has yet been obtained from Boeing or Singapore Airlines.

A photograph taken by aviation photographer Hongming Zheng at Paine Field (PAE) in Washington state on October 10, 2026, records N20092 on the ground. The photo information identifies it as a 777-9, and the photographer notes visible elements of Singapore Airlines' livery and folded wingtips, providing an image record of the aircraft's recent ground activity.

Brake and taxi tests are preflight ground checks used to assess aircraft systems during ground movement, control and deceleration. In the supplied update, October 14 remains a tentative date and must not be treated as confirmation that the aircraft has completed its first flight. The term first flight here refers only to this individual aircraft's maiden flight.

The 777-9 is a large twin-engine widebody aircraft in Boeing's 777X family, featuring GE9X engines and folding wingtips. Boeing's published specifications list a fuselage length of 76.7 meters and an extended wingspan of 71.8 meters, reduced to 64.8 meters with the wingtips folded on the ground. This design balances aerodynamic efficiency with airport ground infrastructure requirements.

An individual production aircraft's first flight does not mean it has been delivered to an airline or is ready for passenger service. In its 2026 update on 777-9 testing, Boeing said production-configured aircraft were supporting certification work alongside dedicated flight-test aircraft, with deliveries expected to begin in 2027 at that time. Further testing, delivery and operational arrangements for WH291 remain subject to official announcements.
